calls.head: The Sabres don’t own Vasilevskiy
calls.body: Vasilevskiy has been shaky against the Sabres since 2023-24, well below his usual. But three seasons of data say a goalie’s record against one team tells us nothing about the next meeting, so don’t be surprised if he looks like himself tonight.
calls.call: If Vasilevskiy starts, his save percentage lands closer to his usual .911 than to his .855 against the Sabres.

calls.head: Where the Lightning have the edge: the penalty kill
calls.body: The Lightning are around the middle of the league for the penalty kill, and the Sabres are around the middle. That’s the biggest gap between these two, and it isn’t a big one.

surprises.head: Tampa Bay got the good looks
surprises.body: Tampa Bay usually gets better looks than most teams. Even by those standards, this was a night of good looks: a 15.1% chance of scoring on the average shot at 5-on-5, against their usual 6.6% and a league average of 6.4%. A team strays this far less than once in a thousand games. You may never see it again.

surprises.head: Tampa Bay brought the hits
surprises.body: Tampa Bay usually hits less than most teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 222 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 89 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far less than once in a thousand games. You may never see it again.

surprises.head: Buffalo flipped the shot count
surprises.body: Tampa Bay controls the shot count like almost no one else. Not tonight: Buffalo took 50 of the 74 shot attempts at 5-on-5. From how these two usually play, Buffalo would expect about 45%. A team strays this far about once every 125 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: A natural hat trick for Kucherov
paras: Sam O'Reilly played his first NHL game and picked up a point. Scott Sabourin and John Carlson scored 49 seconds apart late in the first to put the Lightning up 2-0. It was a busy second period. Brandon Hagel extended the lead to 3-0 early in the period, and Yanni Gourde made it 4-0 midway through the period. The Lightning’s Erik Černák left in the second period and didn’t return. Two days later, he was listed as day to day with an upper-body injury. Josh Doan scored late in the period, and Jason Zucker followed less than four minutes after that to cut Tampa Bay’s lead to 4-2. The third period brought five goals. Tage Thompson made it 4-3 just 33 seconds into the period, but they got no closer. Nikita Kucherov stretched the lead to 5-3, 52 seconds later. Buffalo pulled Ukko-Pekka Luukkonen after five goals and turned to Colten Ellis for the rest of the third. Kucherov struck again early in the third to make it 6-3 for the Lightning. Kucherov completed a natural hat trick on the power play with less than six minutes left to make it 7-3, with Carlson picking up his 800th NHL point on the goal. Hagel scored again 53 seconds later to make it 8-3. Carlson assisted on all three, and had four assists in all. Jake Guentzel finished with four assists, and Hagel added an assist for a three-point night.

The chances were closer than the score. Andrei Vasilevskiy made 28 saves for the Lightning. Nobody on the ice had a bigger night than Charle-Édouard D'Astous, even with Kucherov’s hat trick in the game, by our Swing measure. The Bolts improved to 12-4-2 and climbed to second in the Atlantic, while the Sabres fell to 8-7-3, sixth in the Atlantic.
